subject: Banking
title: Derivatives: Banking's Biggest Bet
description: A short lesson to help you apply Derivatives: Banking's Biggest Bet.

hook.text: The global derivatives market is worth $632 trillion in notional value.

buildup.text: Derivatives are contracts whose value depends on something else: interest rates, currencies, stocks, or commodities.

discovery.text: Banks earn fees structuring custom derivatives for clients. A single interest rate swap can generate millions in fees.

twist.text: In 2008, AIG sold $440 billion in credit default swaps it couldn't pay.

climax.text: Derivatives are insurance contracts that generate fees for banks.

punchline.text: $632 trillion market. Huge fees. But 2008 showed the hidden danger.

quiz.question: What is the notional value of the global derivatives market?

details.summary: Banks earn billions trading derivatives, financial contracts whose value derives from underlying assets like interest rates, currencies, and commodities. The global derivatives market exceeds $600 trillion in notional value.
details.whyItMatters: Derivatives generate enormous profits for banks but also create hidden risks that can threaten the financial system.The 2008 crisis was largely caused by derivatives that spread risk in ways nobody fully understood.
takeaways: The notional value of global derivatives exceeds $600 trillion
The five largest US banks hold over 90 percent of US bank derivatives
Banks earn from the spread between buying and selling derivative contracts

faq.question: How do banks make money from derivatives?
faq.answer: Banks act as dealers, buying derivatives from one client and selling similar ones to another, profiting from the spread. They also earn fees for structuring custom derivative contracts and for providing market-making liquidity.

faq.question: Are derivatives still dangerous after 2008 reforms?
faq.answer: Post-crisis regulations moved most standard derivatives to central clearinghouses and increased capital requirements. However, the market remains enormous and complex, and custom over-the-counter derivatives still carry significant counterparty risk.
